signals.signal: AGM of 28/04/2026 approved a 2026 investment programme of RON 1,017.40m incl. VAT: IT and cards RON 663.17m (IT hardware 34.23, IT software 407.82, retail & cards 221.11 - of which retail/cards HARDWARE 51.92 and retail/cards software 169.19); digital initiatives RON 177.22m; buildings/agencies RON 105.94m; machines RON 21.39m; security RON 9.79m; cash processing centre RON 7.88m; other RON 32.00m. Bank-level 2026 budget: operating income RON 9,786m, operating costs RON 4,344m, net provisions RON 622m, gross profit RON 4,819m.
signals.source_name: BVB/ASF current report - Hotararile AGOA/AGEA Banca Transilvania 28.04.2026
signals.implies: A named, board-approved hardware budget - retail & cards hardware RON 51.92m (~EUR 10.4m), machines RON 21.39m, cash processing centre RON 7.88m, security RON 9.79m - maps directly onto Printec ATM/self-service, cash automation/recyclers, POS hardware and HSM/security. The RON 177.22m digital-initiatives line is the natural home for digital onboarding/eKYC and managed services.
signals.likelihood: High - budget approved and in execution through 2026
signals.followup: Get the 2027 investment programme when tabled (AGM ~Apr-2027) and test whether the retail/cards hardware line rises with a multifunctional-machine roll-out; ask BT procurement who holds the current ATM/recycler frame agreement.

signals.signal: At 30/06/2026 the Bank reports a network of over 2,000 ATMs of which 691 are multifunctional machines, plus 616 BT Express terminals used for operations other than cash withdrawal; over 200,000 installed POS terminals, 51,000 STAR partner locations and over 8,800 e-commerce merchants. Card portfolio 8.5 million; over 5 million unique digitalised customers; over 200,000 new customers in H1-2026, a significant part opening accounts fully digitally through BT Pay with no branch visit.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Financial results 30 June 2026 (interim report filed with BVB/ASF)
signals.implies: Only about 35% of BT's ATM estate is deposit/recycling-capable, leaving roughly 1,300 cash-out-only machines - the largest single cash-automation white space in Romania and a direct recycler opportunity. The 616 BT Express units are a dedicated self-service fleet due for refresh. Fully digital account opening at this volume confirms live eKYC/onboarding and AML-screening demand.
signals.likelihood: High - fleet mix disclosed, refresh cycle ongoing
signals.followup: Pull BT's own ATM locator feed to count deposit-capable sites per city and reconcile against the 691 figure; profile the BT Express estate's vendor and age.

signals.signal: Self-service fleet is contracting within 2026: at 31/03/2026 BT reported 2,025 ATMs of which 696 multifunctional, 632 BT Express terminals, over 188,000 POS, 47,000 STAR locations, 8,400 e-commerce merchants and 8.2m cards. By 30/06/2026 multifunctional machines had fallen to 691 and BT Express to 616, while POS rose to over 200,000, STAR to 51,000, e-commerce merchants to 8,800 and cards to 8.5m.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Rezultate financiare 31 martie 2026 (interim report filed with BVB/ASF)
signals.implies: BT is retiring self-service hardware (-5 multifunctional, -16 BT Express in a single quarter) while acceptance grows - machines are being decommissioned faster than replaced, which is the classic trigger point for a fleet-refresh or ATM-as-a-service tender covering ATM, recycler and BT Express replacement.
signals.followup: Track the Q3-2026 report (due ~Nov-2026): a step-up in the multifunctional count would signal an awarded refresh contract; continued decline signals a run-to-failure estate ripe for a managed-services pitch.

signals.signal: Branch network keeps contracting while headcount grows. At 30/06/2026 the Bank operates its Cluj-Napoca head office plus 42 branches, 463 agencies, 3 work units, 8 healthcare division units, 2 private banking agencies, 1 branch in Italy and 1 Bucharest regional office (31/12/2025: 42 branches, 475 agencies; 31/03/2026: 466 agencies). Group active employees 13,565 at 30/06/2026 versus 13,361 at 31/12/2025.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Financial results 30 June 2026 (interim report filed with BVB/ASF)
signals.implies: Twelve agencies closed in six months while staff numbers rose - cash and service volume must migrate to self-service, the same automation-inside-a-retained-network pattern already seen at CEC Bank. Each closed agency is a candidate site for a recycler or assisted self-service pod, and thins the estate that managed services would cover.
signals.likelihood: High - trend confirmed across three consecutive reporting dates
signals.followup: Map the 12 closed agency locations against BT's ATM locator to see whether a machine was left behind or the site went dark entirely.

signals.signal: H1-2026 results: BT Group net profit RON 2.5bn (+26.8% y/y), Bank net profit RON 2.1bn (+20.7%), Group total assets RON 233.3bn, customer deposits RON 172.4bn, gross loans/deposits 65.9%, operating income RON 5.3bn (+15.9%), cost/income 44.6% at bank level (38.3% excluding the turnover tax), ROE 21.98%, capital adequacy 21.96%, cost of risk 0.63% (-20bp y/y), EPS RON 1.9389 (+24.2%). Around RON 25bn of financing granted in H1; total transactions across all channels up more than 17% y/y; BT Pay mobile payments +24%.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - FactSheet 30 June 2026 (filed with BVB/ASF)
signals.implies: Capital adequacy near 22% and cost/income under 40% ex-tax mean BT has both the money and the efficiency mandate to fund an automation programme; a 17% rise in transaction volume against a shrinking machine fleet is exactly the capacity squeeze recyclers and self-service resolve.
signals.followup: Use the cost/income target (2026 budget guidance 45.6%, 39.4% ex turnover tax) as the ROI frame in any Printec business case.

signals.signal: On the H1-2026 earnings call of 24/08/2026 CFO George Calinescu said the bank continues to invest in technology, cybersecurity, data improvements and artificial intelligence, and guided cost/income to stay flat or improve in H2-2026. The ESG section cites more than 350 ATMs and recycling machines fitted with audio guidance. BT GO has over 600,000 companies enrolled, 86% transactionally active, with 61 million transactions and RON 700bn of payment volume; 36,000 consumer and card loans were originated through BT Pay in H1-2026.
signals.source_name: Investing.com - Earnings call transcript: Banca Transilvania posts strong H1 2026 profit growth
signals.implies: Management explicitly names cybersecurity and technology as protected spend, and confirms BT already operates cash RECYCLING machines (not only deposit ATMs) - so the recycler conversation is a scale-up, not a first sale. Accessibility-fitted machines are a stated ESG commitment, which is a concrete specification hook for a refresh bid.
signals.followup: Obtain BT's own H1-2026 investor presentation (bancatransilvania.ro/.../2026/Semestru-I/Prezentare.pdf) - blocked from this host - to confirm the recycler count and the accessibility figure from primary source.

signals.signal: Law 239/2025, published in Monitorul Oficial no. 1160 of 15/12/2025, amends OUG 193/2002 so that from 01/01/2026 essentially all merchants and service providers registered with the Trade Register - including self-employed persons (PFA) - must accept payment by debit, credit or prepaid card via a POS terminal and/or other modern electronic payment solutions, regardless of annual cash turnover. The previous RON 50,000 turnover threshold is abolished. Refusal is punishable by fines reported at RON 5,000-7,500, and up to RON 15,000 for non-compliance. Entities collecting exclusively through bank accounts with no point-of-sale collection are exempt.
signals.source_name: Legea 239/2025 (Monitorul Oficial 1160/15.12.2025) as reported by Romanian tax and payments trade press (Global Payments Romania, StartupCafe, InfoTVA)
signals.implies: This is the regulatory engine behind BT adding over 12,000 POS terminals in a single quarter. A statutory universal acceptance obligation with fines creates a multi-year, non-discretionary POS/SoftPOS deployment wave across every Romanian acquirer - the largest addressable POS opportunity in the market and the same pattern Printec already meets in Albania.
signals.likelihood: High - already in force and enforced
signals.followup: Verify the exact article and fine bands against the Monitorul Oficial text on legislatie.just.ro (site dropped the connection this run), and size the residual unequipped merchant base with ONRC registration counts against BNR POS totals.

signals.signal: Legislative initiative B409/2026 - 'Propunere legislativa pentru modificarea si completarea Legii nr.209/2019 privind serviciile de plata si pentru modificarea unor acte normative' - was registered at the Senate for debate on 24/06/2026. As reported, it would oblige every payment service provider operating ATMs to let any user enter a personalised withdrawal amount regardless of which bank issued the card, instead of only preset on-screen amounts, with reported fines of RON 50,000-100,000 for non-compliance. The Senate is first chamber; the Chamber of Deputies decides.
signals.source_name: Senatul Romaniei - legislative register, initiative B409/2026
signals.implies: If adopted, every ATM in Romania needs an application-software change and re-certification - a fleet-wide, deadline-driven software and managed-services engagement across BT's 2,000+ machines and the country's 11,136. Printec's ATM software/managed-services line is the direct fit; it also gives a commercial reason to open a fleet conversation with BT before the law lands.
signals.likelihood: Medium in 6-12 months - cross-party sponsorship but still first-chamber stage
signals.followup: Track B409/2026 through the Senate and then cdep.ro; obtain the expunere de motive and any BNR/ARB opinion, and check for a transition period that would set the compliance deadline.

signals.signal: On 02/07/2026 the Romanian data protection authority ANSPDCP concluded an investigation at Banca Transilvania SA, found breaches of Article 32(1),(2) and (4) GDPR and fined the bank EUR 5,000 (RON 26,172). An employee, at a third party's request and outside their duties, accessed a customer's account statements exposing name, IBAN, account type, client code, transaction data and balance. The authority ordered BT to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to prevent unauthorised employee access. The fine has been paid.
signals.source_name: ANSPDCP (Autoritatea Nationala de Supraveghere a Prelucrarii Datelor cu Caracter Personal) - press release
signals.implies: A regulator has formally ordered BT to strengthen internal access controls over customer data - an open, dated corrective-measures obligation. Printec's transaction monitoring, AML/compliance and security tooling (privileged-access and insider-activity monitoring over core banking data) addresses exactly the finding, and the order gives a compliance deadline to sell against.
signals.likelihood: Medium - remediation must be evidenced to the authority
signals.followup: Ask BT compliance what remediation was submitted to ANSPDCP and whether insider-access monitoring was bought or built in-house.

signals.signal: BT's H1-2026 accounts state that its subsidiary Victoriabank SA, notified on 06/07/2020 that it is under investigation by the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Moldova, remains subject to a precautionary seizure placed on some of its assets on 06/08/2020 to cover claims of approximately RON 475 million equivalent at 30/06/2026 - up from approximately RON 450 million equivalent stated at 31/03/2026. No provision is recognised.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Financial results 30 June 2026 (interim report filed with BVB/ASF)
signals.implies: A live, growing financial-crime exposure inside BT Group's Moldovan arm keeps AML/transaction-monitoring investment politically protected at group level. Victoriabank is a separate, smaller estate than BT Romania and a distinct entry point for Printec AML/compliance and monitoring, and for self-service in Moldova.
signals.followup: Profile Victoriabank's own ATM/POS estate and its AML vendor stack; check BNM (Moldova) statistics and Victoriabank's own interim report for machine counts.

signals.signal: BT's H1-2026 risk narrative flags as a named risk 'the increase in cyber risk in the banking sector, driven by accelerated digitalization and growing dependencies on third-party providers and outsourced services, amid an increasingly complex and persistent cyber threat landscape', which may affect operational resilience and continuity of critical financial services.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Financial results 30 June 2026 (interim report filed with BVB/ASF)
signals.implies: BT is publicly naming third-party and outsourcing dependency as a board-level risk - which raises the bar for any managed-services proposal (DORA-grade evidence, exit plans, sub-outsourcing transparency) but also opens the HSM/security and resilience-monitoring conversation. Lead with resilience assurance, not cost.
signals.followup: Obtain BT's DORA third-party register requirements and critical-ICT-provider criteria before pitching any outsourced/managed model.

signals.signal: Chat BT recorded 2.4 million interactions in the period to 30/06/2026, with 82% of interactions resolved without human assistance and 18% routed to a consultant; it is multilingual in Romanian, English, Italian and Hungarian. BT also consolidates an in-house software subsidiary, Code Crafters by BT S.R.L., whose share capital was increased in 2026.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Financial results 30 June 2026 (interim report filed with BVB/ASF)
signals.implies: BT automates its service layer in-house and is funding its own software arm - a build-not-buy bias that makes a front-end digital pitch hard. Printec's realistic opening is the regulated plumbing behind the assistant: eKYC/identity verification, AML screening and transaction monitoring, plus the physical self-service layer the software arm does not make.
signals.followup: Establish what Code Crafters by BT builds versus what BT buys, to route the pitch away from anything they in-source.

signals.signal: On 06/08/2026 BRD extended the RoPay service in its YOU BRD app so that individuals and PFAs can make instant account-to-account payments to merchants and service providers in physical stores, on online platforms, and by scanning QR codes from invoices and from POS terminals, without using a bank card, with funds transferred in real time to RON current accounts and no fee to BRD customers. RoPay runs on the Instant Payments infrastructure operated by TRANSFOND with the Romanian Banks Association; ten banks including Banca Transilvania participate. BT Pay already supports scanning RoPay QR codes at POS and at cash registers.
signals.source_name: Profit.ro / Bursa.ro - BRD extends RoPay instant payments to merchants
signals.implies: Account-to-account QR is now moving onto the POS estate itself in Romania. For Printec this cuts both ways: it pressures card-acquiring economics, but it also means POS terminals must display and reconcile QR alongside card - a software/terminal-capability refresh across every acquirer's fleet, and a reason for BT to touch its 200,000 terminals.
signals.likelihood: High - already launched at a top-3 bank
signals.followup: Confirm from a primary BT source whether BT has launched RoPay merchant acceptance for its own merchant base (BT's own newsroom is blocked from this host); check TRANSFOND for RoPay merchant transaction volumes.

signals.signal: BNR payment indicators reported for 31/12/2025: 11,136 ATMs operated by resident payment service providers (up 1,108 versus June 2025), 729,408 POS terminals (up 161,396), 685,731 EFTPOS points (up 120,300) and 28.63 million active cards (up 10.07% versus June 2025), of which 24.68 million with cash withdrawal functionality.
signals.source_name: BNR payment indicators as reported by Bursa.ro
signals.implies: Sets the denominator: BT's 2,000+ ATMs are roughly a fifth of the national estate and its 200,000+ POS roughly a quarter of national POS, so BT is the single largest self-service and acceptance account in Romania. National ATM count is still growing, which contradicts the pan-CEE branch/ATM shrinkage narrative and argues for a growth rather than rationalisation pitch in this market.
signals.followup: Re-source these figures from BNR primary (the Indicatori plati page 302-redirects to the homepage from this host) and obtain the H1-2026 update when published.

coverage_notes: Fresh run - no checkpoint existed. Searched English and Romanian across primary IR/exchange filings (BVB infocont: AGM resolutions 28/04/2026, Q1 report 22/05/2026, H1 report and FactSheet 21/08/2026), regulator registers new to this beat (senat.ro legislative register, dataprotection.ro/ANSPDCP), the H1 earnings-call transcript, Romanian fiscal/payments trade press, and the RoPay/TRANSFOND instant-payments environment. All PDFs were extracted locally with pdfminer rather than trusted to the fetch tool's summary. Three explicit corrections to the brief's framing: (1) the OTP Bank Romania merger is NOT a 2026 event - it completed 28/02/2025 and appears in H1-2026 only as a prior-year comparative footnote, so it should not be briefed as live; (2) the aggregator figures circulating for BT ('1,800 ATMs / 550 multifunctional', '470 BT Express', '150,000 POS', '1,770 ATMs / 81,700 POS') are stale - the 2022-vintage and undated ones are superseded by the primary 31/03/2026 and 30/06/2026 filings used here, and should not be carried forward; (3) BT's POS growth is regulatory in origin (Law 239/2025) rather than commercial. Genuine gaps: BT's own H1-2026 investor presentation was never opened (host blocked), so the '350+ ATMs and recycling machines with audio guidance' figure rests on the earnings-call transcript only and is tagged press; BT's ATM locator feed was not pulled for a deposit-capable site count because the whole domain is blocked from this host; BNR payment indicators could not be taken from primary; no ATM/recycler vendor incumbency for BT could be established from any source this run (unlike BCR, where NCR Atleos names Printec as channel partner) - that remains an open question worth a targeted operator check.
